newsitem.title: POLAND: JAPANESE WOMEN WIN HONOURS IN POLISH VIOLIN CONTEST.
newsitem.headline: JAPANESE WOMEN WIN HONOURS IN POLISH VIOLIN CONTEST.

text.p: Two young Japanese women captured high honours at Poland's prestigious international violin competition, but no first prize was awarded, PAP news agency said on Sunday.
The judges' panel of the Wieniawski International Violin Competition in the western city of Poznan deliberated late into the night before deciding that no violinist merited first place.
Reiko Otani, 23, and Akiko Tanaka, 26, won the second and third prizes respectively, and two identical fourth prizes went to Pole Lukasz Blaszczyk, 25, and Japanese woman Asuka Sezaki, 19.
Two Polish women, 17-year-old Anna Reszniak and Maria Nowak, 19, came in fifth and sixth respectively.
Otani will be the soloist at a gala concert on Monday, directed by Britain's renowned violin virtuoso, Sir Yehudi Menuhin.
The competition, named after Polish 19th-century composer Henryk Wieniawski, originated in 1935 and is held in Poznan every five years.
For many aspiring young violinists, winning a prize at the event has traditionally been a springboard to a major music career.
